model.name: File detail: buttons and preview first, metadata last
model.description: The in-room file detail view is reordered so action buttons (open-in-preview, open-in-new-tab) come first at the top, then a pan- and zoom-capable preview pane sized at 75% of screen height, then the metadata detail (name, size, type, scenario info) last - reversed from the current order where detail is on top and buttons/preview are at the bottom.
model.tronQuote: > TRON: "the in room file details shall START with the action button and the preview pane, then the detail. reverse order. preview 75% screen size. preview needs to pan zoom its content."

acceptanceCriteria.text: The file detail view renders three sections in this order top to bottom: [action buttons] -> [preview pane] -> [metadata detail].
Action buttons (open-in-preview, open-in-new-tab) are the FIRST/top section.
Metadata detail (name, size, type, scenario info) is the LAST/bottom section, below the preview.
Order is REVERSED from the current layout (was: metadata top, buttons+preview bottom).
The preview pane is the MIDDLE section, sized at height: 75vh (75% of viewport height).
Desktop: pointer/wheel zoom on the preview content (scroll-zoom).
Mobile/touch: pinch-zoom on the preview content.
Zoom uses CSS transform with transform-origin anchored at the pointer/pinch focal point (zoom toward cursor/fingers, not a fixed corner).
Content can be PANNED (dragged) while zoomed in; pan is bounded to the content extent.
Bounded-overlay discipline: the pane height is bounded and element bounds == visible bounds, so the preview never eats taps/clicks outside its 75vh box.
Pan/zoom is encapsulated in a reusable web component rb-preview-pane (not inlined per-call), with gesture handling built in.
rb-preview-pane exposes a content slot/attr and the consumer (rb-file-detail) only places it between buttons and metadata; gestures are the component's responsibility.
rb-preview-pane is reusable beyond file-detail (any 75vh-bounded pan/zoom surface) — no file-detail-specific coupling in the component.
Image content renders in the preview and pans/zooms.
Text content renders in the preview and pans/zooms (scrollable + zoomable).
PDF content renders in the preview and pans/zooms.
URL content renders (embedded/preview) in the pane; open-in-new-tab button still available.

testScenarios.name: DOM order reversed
testScenarios.given: a file detail view for any file
testScenarios.then: querying the section order yields [buttons, preview, metadata] top-to-bottom; buttons are first, metadata last (reversed from the prior metadata-first layout)

testScenarios.name: preview 75vh
testScenarios.then: its computed height === 75vh (75% of viewport height)

testScenarios.name: desktop scroll-zoom toward cursor
testScenarios.given: the preview rendered on desktop with content loaded
testScenarios.when: a wheel event fires over a point P
testScenarios.then: the content scale increases and transform-origin is anchored at P (content under the cursor stays under the cursor)

testScenarios.name: mobile pinch-zoom
testScenarios.given: the preview rendered on touch with content loaded
testScenarios.then: the content scales with transform-origin at the pinch focal midpoint

testScenarios.name: pan while zoomed, bounded
testScenarios.then: the content pans and cannot be dragged beyond its own extent (bounded)

testScenarios.name: bounded overlay does not steal taps
testScenarios.when: a tap/click lands outside the pane bounds
testScenarios.then: the event reaches the element below; the preview only handles events within its visible 75vh box

testScenarios.name: rb-preview-pane component
testScenarios.then: the preview is an rb-preview-pane custom element with built-in gesture handling; rb-file-detail does not implement gestures itself; the component carries no file-detail-specific coupling

testScenarios.name: all content types render + gesture
testScenarios.given: files of type image, text, PDF, and URL
testScenarios.when: each is opened in the preview
testScenarios.then: each renders in rb-preview-pane; image/text/PDF pan+zoom; URL renders with open-in-new-tab still available
